feature: Design records are checked by tests
description: The repository's own tests check that the spec-first process left its records: specs for accepted ADRs, acceptance records, bound tests with red commits, CI running mypy and pytest, and no stray dot files.

specs.description: An Accepted ADR with a matching spec passes
specs.given: docs/adrs/ holds ADR-2611221115 with status Accepted, and docs/specs/ADR-2611221115.json exists with adr field "ADR-2611221115"
specs.then: it reports no failure for ADR-2611221115

specs.description: Proposed and superseded ADRs need no spec
specs.given: docs/adrs/ holds one ADR with status Proposed and ADR-2611221107 with status Superseded, and neither has a spec
specs.then: it reports no failure for either ADR

specs.description: A Completed ADR without a spec is refused
specs.given: docs/adrs/ holds an ADR with status Completed and docs/specs/ has no file named after its id
specs.then: it fails and names that ADR as missing its spec

specs.description: A spec whose adr field names a different ADR is refused
specs.given: an Accepted ADR-A has docs/specs/ADR-A.json, but that file's adr field is "ADR-B"
specs.then: it fails and names ADR-A's spec as naming the wrong ADR

specs.description: ADR-2611221107 is the only exemption
specs.given: an Accepted ADR other than ADR-2611221107 has no spec
specs.then: it fails for that ADR. The exemption does not extend to any other id.

specs.description: Every accepted or completed ADR except the exempt one has its own spec
specs.given: any set of ADRs in docs/adrs/ with any statuses, and any set of spec files
specs.then: it passes if and only if, for every ADR other than ADR-2611221107 whose status is Accepted or Completed, docs/specs/<id>.json exists and its adr field equals <id>

specs.description: A bound spec with a full acceptance record passes
specs.given: a spec binds one scenario to a test and has accepted {"by": "C. Johns", "sha256": <64 lowercase hex characters>}
specs.then: it reports no acceptance failure for that spec

specs.description: A spec with no bound scenarios needs no acceptance
specs.given: a spec in which no scenario has a test field and no accepted record exists
specs.then: it reports no acceptance failure for that spec

specs.description: A bound spec with no accepted record is refused
specs.given: a spec binds a scenario to a test and has no accepted field
specs.then: it fails and names that spec as unaccepted

specs.description: An empty acceptor is refused
specs.given: a spec binds a scenario to a test and its accepted.by is ""
specs.then: it fails for that spec

specs.description: A malformed hash is refused
specs.given: a spec binds a scenario to a test and its accepted.sha256 has 63 characters, or 64 characters including a non-hex character such as "g"
specs.then: it fails for that spec

specs.description: Acceptance is required exactly when something is bound
specs.given: any spec
specs.then: if any scenario in the spec has a test field, the check passes for §2 only when accepted.by is a non-empty string and accepted.sha256 matches ^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$. A spec with no bound scenario never fails §2.

specs.description: A scenario bound to an existing test with a red commit passes
specs.given: a scenario has test "tests/unit/test_design_records.py::test_every_accepted_adr_has_a_spec" and red "a1b2c3d", and that file defines a function of that name
specs.then: it reports no binding failure for that scenario

specs.description: A renamed test is refused
specs.given: a scenario names tests/unit/test_x.py::test_old, and the file exists but defines no function test_old
specs.then: it fails and names the scenario and the missing function

specs.description: A test file outside tests/ or missing is refused
specs.given: a scenario names src/check.py::test_a, or tests/unit/test_gone.py::test_a where that file does not exist
specs.then: it fails for that scenario

specs.description: A missing or malformed red commit is refused
specs.given: a scenario bound to an existing test has no red field, or red "a1b2c3" (6 characters), or a 41-character value, or "zzzzzzz"
specs.then: it fails for that scenario

specs.description: Every binding resolves and carries a red commit id
specs.given: any set of specs with any scenarios
specs.then: it passes §3 if and only if every scenario with a test field "<file>::<function>" has <file> under tests/ that exists and defines a test function named <function>, and has red matching ^[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}$. Scenarios without a test field never fail §3.

specs.description: A workflow that runs both tools on push and pull request passes
specs.given: .github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on push to the default branch and on pull_request, and its steps run "uv run mypy" and "uv run pytest"
specs.then: it reports no CI failure

specs.description: A workflow missing the type checker is refused
specs.given: ci.yml runs "uv run pytest" but no step runs "uv run mypy"
specs.then: it fails and names mypy as missing

specs.description: A workflow missing the test suite is refused
specs.given: ci.yml runs "uv run mypy" but no step runs "uv run pytest"
specs.then: it fails and names pytest as missing

specs.description: A workflow that does not run on pull requests is refused
specs.given: ci.yml triggers only on push to the default branch
specs.then: it fails and names the missing pull_request trigger

specs.description: A missing workflow is refused
specs.given: .github/workflows/ci.yml does not exist
specs.then: it fails

specs.description: Only the allowed dot paths are tracked
specs.given: git ls-files lists .gitattributes, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .gitignore, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .python-version, src/... and tests/...
specs.then: it reports no dot-path failure

specs.description: A committed tool folder is refused
specs.given: git ls-files lists .vscode/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json
specs.then: it fails and names that first segment

specs.description: A near-match of an allowed name is refused
specs.given: git ls-files lists .python-version.bak or .github-old/x
specs.then: it fails for that path. Allowed names match the whole first segment, not a prefix.

specs.description: Dot files below the top level are not restricted
specs.given: git ls-files lists tests/fixtures/.keep
specs.then: it reports no dot-path failure, because the path's first segment is tests

specs.description: The set of tracked dot segments is a subset of the allow-list
specs.given: any list of tracked paths from git ls-files
specs.then: it passes §5 if and only if the first path segment of every path that starts with "." is one of .gitattributes, .github, .gitignore, .pre-commit-config.yaml, .python-version

amendments.reason: S12's property names ^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$; add a 65-character hash case, which a mutation (search for fullmatch) showed the test did not cover
read tracked paths with git ls-files -z: plain ls-files quotes a non-ASCII path, which then escapes the §5 dot-segment check; review finding
